topic_title: The Secret Pact That Carved Up Europe

slides.headline: Hitler and Stalin Secretly Split Europe
slides.body: In 1939, two dictators signed a public peace deal — and a hidden map dividing Poland and the Baltics between them.

slides.headline: Moscow, August 1939
slides.body: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed a non-aggression pact days before invading Poland — publicly, a promise of peace.

slides.headline: A Secret Clause Divided Two Nations
slides.body: Behind closed doors, Molotov and Ribbentrop signed a secret protocol carving Poland and the Baltic states between Berlin and Moscow.

slides.headline: The USSR Denied It for 50 Years
slides.body: Moscow called the protocol a forgery until 1989, when its own Congress admitted the document was real — and void from the start.
slides.source: USSR Congress of People's Deputies, Dec 1989

slides.headline: Great Powers Trade Nations Like Currency
slides.body: Two regimes shook hands in public and carved up sovereign countries in private. The people living there were never asked.

slides.headline: What Other Peace Deals Hide a Map?
slides.body: One secret line on a map decided the fate of millions before a single shot was fired. How many maps are still hidden?
